ov: One of the most diverse lizard families, with more than 1,500 species. Most skinks have small legs and hardly any neck, and some have no limbs at all. Many can shed their tail to escape a predator and regrow it in about three to four months.
rg: Almost worldwide, in every kind of habitat except arctic and subarctic regions.
df: Mostly insects such as flies, crickets, grasshoppers, beetles and caterpillars; some species kept as pets are omnivores.
fx: About 45% of skink species give birth to live young, and a few nourish them through a placenta.
Blue-tongued skinks of Australia and New Guinea bare their large blue tongue as a bluff warning.
